headline: High: Firecrawl’s broad egress and API-key handling create default data-leak and compliance risk when paired with a content-writing agent that can ingest web content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing agent with no documented isolation or input filters, while firecrawl can fetch arbitrary web content via broad network egress and MCP-compatible/API surfaces. If Firecrawl output is copied into the writer, prompt injection is plausible in default workflows. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Firecrawl-sourced text is pasted or piped into the content-writing workflow
IF the writer treats fetched content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed instruction/data separator in the prompt template
Strip HTML/markdown comments and hidden text before handoff
Require a human review step before any tool-using follow-up
Use a denylist for instruction-like phrases in fetched content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from fetch to render

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys, and it has broad egress plus API/MCP access. awesome-cli-apps has no documented data handling controls, so if both share a workspace or prompt context, sensitive material can flow from B into A’s outputs or logs. The shared-pathway is inferred from profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied prompt context
IF Firecrawl processes pages containing secrets or screenshots with sensitive content
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs in a separate directory
Redact API keys and secrets before any handoff
Disable verbose logging for fetched pages
Review prompts for embedded sensitive snippets before reuse
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping filesystem write, git, or database mutation rights. Firecrawl supports multiple instances and API/CLI use; awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing agent with no write surface documented. A real write conflict is not evidenced, so only a low-risk overlap remains.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF future configuration adds shared filesystem or git writes
mitigations: Run the agents in separate working directories
Avoid shared mutable state during concurrent runs
Serialize any writes through one coordinator
Check for accidental git or file writes in dry runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl can produce scraped content and structured data, and awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing agent that may render or reuse that output. There is no documented verification step between them, so A’s output can become B’s input with no guardrail. The downstream harm is usually incorrect content rather than irreversible action, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is fed into the writer without fact-checking
IF the writer republishes scraped claims as authoritative text
mitigations: Insert a verification checklist before reuse
Require source links alongside extracted claims
Mark scraped text as untrusted in the prompt
Limit downstream use to draft-only outputs
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and web content, while awesome-cli-apps has no documented retention, residency, or subject-rights controls. If the pair processes regulated or sensitive web data, the mismatch in documented compliance posture creates a plausible breach path. Because only B has concrete sensitive-data handling evidence, the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII or secrets is processed through Firecrawl
IF the pair is used in an environment requiring retention or deletion guarantees
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention and deletion expectations before use
Separate secret-bearing jobs from content-writing jobs
Review logs for stored page content and keys
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
